passages.pull_quote: He will make your paths straight.

passages.text: and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
passages.pull_quote: This is the way. Walk in it.

passages.text: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.
passages.pull_quote: He will guide the humble in justice.

passages.text: However, when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.
passages.pull_quote: He will guide you into all truth.

passages.text: and the LORD will guide you continually, satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong. You will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters don’t fail.
passages.pull_quote: The LORD will guide you continually.

passages.text: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
passages.pull_quote: By his wounds we are healed.

passages.text: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed toward us.
passages.pull_quote: Not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed.

passages.text: Therefore my spirit is overwhelmed within me. My heart within me is desolate.
passages.pull_quote: My spirit is overwhelmed within me.

passages.text: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.
passages.pull_quote: Hope in God! For I shall still praise him.

passages.text: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
passages.pull_quote: Looking for the blessed hope.

passages.text: Now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
passages.pull_quote: My hope is in you.

passages.text: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.
passages.pull_quote: Don't let your heart be troubled.

passages.text: The LORD has done great things for us, and we are glad.
passages.pull_quote: The LORD has done great things for us, and we are glad.

passages.text: You have put gladness in my heart, more than when their grain and their new wine are increased.
passages.pull_quote: You have put gladness in my heart.

passages.text: For even though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines, the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food, the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls, yet I will rejoice in the LORD. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
passages.pull_quote: I will rejoice in the LORD.

passages.text: whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,
passages.pull_quote: You rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable.

passages.text: Don’t fret because of evildoers, neither be envious against those who work unrighteousness.
passages.pull_quote: Don't fret because of evildoers, neither be envious.

passages.text: Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear the LORD all day long.
passages.pull_quote: Don't let your heart envy sinners.

passages.text: For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
passages.pull_quote: Living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.

passages.text: Putting away therefore all wickedness, all deceit, hypocrisies, envies, and all evil speaking,
passages.pull_quote: Putting away therefore all wickedness... envies.

passages.text: But as for me, my feet were almost gone. My steps had nearly slipped. For I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
passages.pull_quote: I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

passages.text: Then I saw all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
passages.pull_quote: All the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man's neighbor.

passages.text: but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.
passages.pull_quote: Everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

passages.text: For this is the will of God: your sanctification, that you abstain from sexual immorality, that each one of you know how to control his own body in sanctification and honor, not in the passion of lust, even as the Gentiles who don’t know God,
passages.pull_quote: That you abstain from sexual immorality.

passages.text: Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart, neither let her captivate you with her eyelids.
passages.pull_quote: Don't lust after her beauty in your heart.

passages.text: Flee from youthful lusts; but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
passages.pull_quote: Flee from youthful lusts; but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace.

passages.text: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.
passages.pull_quote: Make no provision for the flesh, for its lusts.

passages.text: Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things. Revive me in your ways.
passages.pull_quote: Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things.

passages.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
passages.pull_quote: Greater love has no one than this.

passages.text: Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God. He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
passages.pull_quote: God is love.

passages.text: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor that which is evil. Cling to that which is good. In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor prefer one another,
passages.pull_quote: Let love be without hypocrisy.

passages.text: Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
passages.pull_quote: Walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.

passages.text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.
passages.pull_quote: Love never fails.

passages.text: A man’s pride brings him low, but one of lowly spirit gains honor.
passages.pull_quote: A man's pride brings him low, but one of lowly spirit gains honor.

passages.text: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.” Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
passages.pull_quote: God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.

passages.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
passages.pull_quote: Whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

passages.text: For I say through the grace that was given me, to everyone who is among you, not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.
passages.pull_quote: Not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think.

passages.text: The LORD says, “Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom. Don’t let the mighty man glory in his might. Don’t let the rich man glory in his riches. But let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am the LORD who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness on the earth, for I delight in these things,” says the LORD.
passages.pull_quote: Let him who glories glory in this, that he understands and knows me.

passages.text: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
passages.pull_quote: If you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

passages.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
passages.pull_quote: Not seven times, but seventy times seven.

passages.text: Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice. And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
passages.pull_quote: Forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

passages.text: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.
passages.pull_quote: Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.

passages.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
passages.pull_quote: Love your enemies, bless those who curse you.

passages.text: looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and many be defiled by it,
passages.pull_quote: Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.

passages.text: Hurry to answer me, the LORD. My spirit fails. Don’t hide your face from me, so that I don’t become like those who go down into the pit. Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
passages.pull_quote: Hurry to answer me, LORD. My spirit fails.

passages.text: Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the bitterness. My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me. This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope. It is because of the LORD’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his mercies don’t fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
passages.pull_quote: His compassions don't fail. They are new every morning.

passages.text: The LORD, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you. Let my prayer enter into your presence. Turn your ear to my cry. For my soul is full of troubles. My life draws near to Sheol.
passages.pull_quote: I have cried day and night before you.

passages.text: For we don’t desire to have you uninformed, brothers, concerning our affliction which happened to us in Asia: that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, so much that we despaired even of life. Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,
passages.pull_quote: We should not trust in ourselves, but in God.

passages.text: Have mercy on me, the LORD, for I am faint. The LORD, heal me, for my bones are troubled. My soul is also in great anguish. But you, the LORD—how long?
passages.pull_quote: Have mercy on me, LORD, for I am faint.

passages.text: Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
passages.pull_quote: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

passages.text: not lagging in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord,
passages.pull_quote: Not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.

passages.text: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
passages.pull_quote: In all hard work there is profit.

passages.text: Whether therefore you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
passages.pull_quote: Do all to the glory of God.

passages.text: Don’t trust in a neighbor. Don’t put confidence in a friend. With the woman lying in your embrace, be careful of the words of your mouth! For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are the men of his own house. But as for me, I will look to the LORD. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
passages.pull_quote: But as for me, I will look to the LORD.

passages.text: When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”
passages.pull_quote: One of you will betray me.

passages.text: Immediately he came to Jesus, and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him. Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then they came and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
passages.pull_quote: Friend, why are you here?

passages.text: Because of all my adversaries I have become utterly contemptible to my neighbors, a horror to my acquaintances. Those who saw me on the street fled from me. I am forgotten from their hearts like a dead man. I am like broken pottery. For I have heard the slander of many, terror on every side, while they conspire together against me, they plot to take away my life. But I trust in you, the LORD. I said, “You are my God.”
passages.pull_quote: But I trust in you, LORD.

passages.text: “He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me. My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me. Those who dwell in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I am an alien in their sight. I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth. My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother. Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me. All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.
passages.pull_quote: All my familiar friends abhor me.

passages.text: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God,
passages.pull_quote: Our sufficiency is from God.

passages.text: The LORD, you have searched me, and you know me. You know my sitting down and my rising up. You perceive my thoughts from afar. You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.
passages.pull_quote: You have searched me, and you know me.

passages.text: For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!” The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;
passages.pull_quote: The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God.

passages.text: So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
passages.pull_quote: The Lord is my helper. I will not fear.

passages.text: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
passages.pull_quote: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver.

passages.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out. But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.
passages.pull_quote: Godliness with contentment is great gain.

passages.text: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly. He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’ He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.” ’ “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’ So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
passages.pull_quote: You fool, tonight your soul is required of you.

passages.text: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty. The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
passages.pull_quote: The liberal soul shall be made fat.

passages.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.” But when the young man heard this, he went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.
passages.pull_quote: He went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.

passages.text: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
passages.pull_quote: God loves a cheerful giver.

passages.text: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
passages.pull_quote: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor.

passages.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it, because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
passages.pull_quote: Though it takes time, wait for it, because it will surely come.

passages.text: The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him. It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.
passages.pull_quote: The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.

passages.text: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
passages.pull_quote: The testing of your faith produces endurance.

passages.text: The LORD assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure. The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.
passages.pull_quote: The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.

passages.text: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
passages.pull_quote: Power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.

passages.text: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me, lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is the LORD?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
passages.pull_quote: Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me.

passages.text: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
passages.pull_quote: Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.

passages.text: The LORD, my heart isn’t arrogant, nor my eyes lofty; nor do I concern myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me. Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
passages.pull_quote: I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother.

passages.text: Beloved, don’t be astonished at the fiery trial which has come upon you to test you, as though a strange thing happened to you. But because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, that at the revelation of his glory you also may rejoice with exceeding joy.
passages.pull_quote: Because you are partakers of Christ's sufferings, rejoice.

passages.text: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
passages.pull_quote: After you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.

passages.text: Because it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer on his behalf,
passages.pull_quote: It has been granted to you on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer on his behalf.

passages.text: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit. Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all.
passages.pull_quote: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.

passages.text: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide their face; and we didn’t respect him. Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted. But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
passages.pull_quote: By his wounds we are healed.

passages.text: They heard the LORD God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden. The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?” The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
passages.pull_quote: I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.

passages.text: They looked to him, and were radiant. Their faces shall never be covered with shame.
passages.pull_quote: They looked to him, and were radiant. Their faces shall never be covered with shame.

passages.text: My God, I have trusted in you. Don’t let me be shamed. Don’t let my enemies triumph over me. Yes, no one who waits for you will be shamed. They will be shamed who deal treacherously without cause.
passages.pull_quote: No one who waits for you will be shamed.

passages.text: Instead of your shame you will have double. Instead of dishonor, they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them.
passages.pull_quote: Instead of your shame you will have double.

passages.text: Behold, at that time I will deal with all those who afflict you; and I will save those who are lame and gather those who were driven away. I will give them praise and honor, whose shame has been in all the earth. At that time I will bring you in, and at that time I will gather you; for I will give you honor and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the LORD.
passages.pull_quote: I will give them praise and honor, whose shame has been in all the earth.

passages.text: You will have plenty to eat and be satisfied, and will praise the name of the LORD, your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my people will never again be disappointed. You will know that I am among Israel, and that I am the LORD, your God, and there is no one else; and my people will never again be disappointed.
passages.pull_quote: My people will never again be disappointed.

passages.text: For the Scripture says, “Whoever believes in him will not be disappointed.”
passages.pull_quote: Whoever believes in him will not be disappointed.

passages.text: For this cause I also suffer these things. Yet I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day.
passages.pull_quote: I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed.

passages.text: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
passages.pull_quote: Who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame.

passages.text: How long, the LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me? How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day? How long shall my enemy triumph over me?
passages.pull_quote: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day?

passages.text: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
passages.pull_quote: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance.

passages.text: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
passages.pull_quote: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.

passages.text: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy. A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world. Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
passages.pull_quote: You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

passages.text: Those ransomed by the LORD will return, and come with singing to Zion. Everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
passages.pull_quote: Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

passages.text: You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, you will let me live. You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth. Increase my honor and comfort me again.
passages.pull_quote: You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth.

passages.text: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we remembered Zion. On the willows in that land, we hung up our harps.
passages.pull_quote: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we remembered Zion.

passages.text: They traveled from Mount Hor by the way to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. The soul of the people was very discouraged because of the journey. The people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, there is no water, and our soul loathes this disgusting food!”
passages.pull_quote: The soul of the people was very discouraged because of the journey.

passages.text: But you be strong! Don’t let your hands be slack, for your work will be rewarded.”
passages.pull_quote: Don't let your hands be slack, for your work will be rewarded.

passages.text: I looked, and rose up, and said to the nobles, to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, “Don’t be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
passages.pull_quote: Don't be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, and fight.

passages.text: Therefore, seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.
passages.pull_quote: Seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don't faint.

passages.text: For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
passages.pull_quote: Consider him who has endured such contradiction, that you don't grow weary, fainting in your souls.

passages.text: Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees, and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
passages.pull_quote: Lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees.

passages.text: You have removed my soul far away from peace. I forgot prosperity. I said, “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from the LORD.”
passages.pull_quote: My strength has perished, along with my expectation from the LORD.

passages.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
passages.pull_quote: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.

passages.text: where then is my hope? As for my hope, who will see it?
passages.pull_quote: Where then is my hope?

passages.text: Then he said to me, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, ‘Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost. We are completely cut off.’ Therefore prophesy, and tell them, ‘The Lord the LORD says: “Behold, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, my people; and I will bring you into the land of Israel. You will know that I am the LORD, when I have opened your graves and caused you to come up out of your graves, my people. I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live. Then I will place you in your own land; and you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken it and performed it,” says the LORD.’ ”
passages.pull_quote: Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost. We are completely cut off.

passages.text: Out of the depths I have cried to you, the LORD. Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my petitions.
passages.pull_quote: Out of the depths I have cried to you, the LORD.

passages.text: Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.”
passages.pull_quote: Against hope, Abraham in hope believed.

passages.text: in hope of eternal life, which God, who can’t lie, promised before time began;
passages.pull_quote: In hope of eternal life, which God, who can't lie, promised before time began.

passages.text: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
passages.pull_quote: Through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

passages.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
passages.pull_quote: Caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

passages.text: I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
passages.pull_quote: I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.

passages.text: He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.
passages.pull_quote: He came to his own, and those who were his own didn't receive him.

passages.text: The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
passages.pull_quote: The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

passages.text: Come to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.
passages.pull_quote: A living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
passages.pull_quote: A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country.

passages.text: The LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they tell you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me as the king over them.
passages.pull_quote: They have not rejected you, but they have rejected me as the king over them.

passages.text: you whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant. I have chosen you and have not cast you away.’
passages.pull_quote: I have chosen you and have not cast you away.

passages.text: I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother’s children.
passages.pull_quote: I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother's children.

passages.text: Therefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered outside of the gate. Let’s therefore go out to him outside of the camp, bearing his reproach.
passages.pull_quote: Let's go out to him outside of the camp, bearing his reproach.

passages.text: having predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his desire, to the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he freely gave us favor in the Beloved.
passages.pull_quote: Having predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ to himself.

passages.text: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.
passages.pull_quote: Accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you.

entries.reflection: Notice what is not promised. The danger does not disappear, and Isaiah does not tell his people that their fear is unreasonable. What changes is that they are no longer alone inside it. Courage here is not the absence of fear but the presence of God within it.
entries.prayer: Lord, be near me in the thing I am afraid of tonight. Steady my heart, and go before me into it.

entries.reflection: David writes this as a soldier, not as a man in safety. He does not deny that there are enemies; he measures them against someone larger. Fear shrinks not when the threat is small but when what stands beside you is greater than it.
entries.prayer: Lord, you are my light. Make me brave enough for the next small step, and only that one.
entries.saint_quote: Let nothing disturb you. Whoever has God lacks nothing.

entries.reflection: Anxiety is care with nowhere to put itself. Peter does not ask you to feel less or to care less. He asks you to hand the weight to someone able to carry it, which is a different action entirely from trying to stop thinking about it.
entries.prayer: Father, I give you the thing I keep turning over. Take it from me, and let me rest tonight.

entries.reflection: Paul replaces worry with a specific action rather than a mood. Name the thing. Ask for it plainly. Vague dread has no edges and so cannot be put down, but a concrete request can be handed over. The peace he describes arrives after the asking, not before it.
entries.prayer: Lord, here is exactly what worries me, said plainly. I place it in your hands and leave it there.

entries.reflection: Grief is not a failure of faith. Christ calls the one who mourns blessed, which means your sorrow is held rather than hurried. The comfort is promised in the future tense; you are not late for it if it has not arrived yet.
entries.prayer: Lord, sit with me in this loss. Comfort me in your time, not in mine.

entries.reflection: Nearness comes before healing in this verse, and that order matters. God draws closest to the broken rather than to the composed, which means you do not have to pull yourself together first in order to be met.
entries.prayer: Jesus, stay close tonight. I do not need answers yet, only your presence.

entries.reflection: Two things are said here, and the second is the useful one. The pull you feel is common to everyone, so it is not evidence that you are uniquely broken. And there is always a way out already made. Look for the exit rather than for more willpower.
entries.prayer: Lord, show me the way out you have already made. Give me strength for the next hour, not the next year.

entries.reflection: Christ names the pattern the night before he dies. Watchfulness comes before the moment, not during it. By the time you are at the edge the fight is mostly decided, so the work belongs earlier, in guarding the approach.
entries.prayer: Jesus, guard my steps before I reach the edge. Make me honest about what leads me there.

entries.reflection: Christ says this hours before his arrest, to men about to scatter. He does not promise you will feel accompanied right away. He promises he will not leave you as an orphan — the loneliness is real, but it is not the last word.
entries.prayer: Jesus, in this empty room, let me know you are here.

entries.reflection: These are the last words of the Gospel, spoken as a command to go out into the world. The promise of presence isn't reserved for the safe moments — always includes the days you feel most alone. It is a fact to lean on, not a feeling to chase.
entries.prayer: Lord, remind me today that I am accompanied, even when it doesn't feel like it.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't condemn the anger itself, only what you let it become after dark. Something in you may be right to be upset. The instruction isn't to swallow it — it's to not let it move in and set up permanent residence.
entries.prayer: Lord, I am angry. Show me what's just in it, and help me set the rest down before tonight.

entries.reflection: The order in this sentence is the whole instruction: hearing first, speaking second, anger last. Most arguments run the order backwards. Listening all the way through, before responding, does more to defuse anger than any amount of self-control applied afterward.
entries.prayer: Lord, slow me down. Let me hear before I answer.

entries.reflection: John doesn't say confession makes the guilt disappear instantly, or that what happened was somehow excusable. He says God is faithful to forgive it — faithful, not merely willing, as though this were a surprising grace rather than routine reluctance you have to talk him into.
entries.prayer: Lord, I bring you what I've done. Forgive me, and help me believe that you already have.

entries.reflection: Paul isn't describing a feeling here but a standing: no condemnation, present tense, for anyone in Christ. Shame keeps re-litigating a case that's already been decided in your favor. You're allowed to stop arguing it.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me live like someone who has actually been forgiven, not like someone still on trial.

entries.reflection: A father says this to Jesus about his own dying son, and it's not a tidy statement of faith. It's two true things said in the same breath: I believe, and I don't believe enough. Christ doesn't ask him to resolve the contradiction first. He heals the boy anyway.
entries.prayer: Lord, I believe. Help my unbelief.

entries.reflection: Thomas gets the encounter he demanded, and Christ doesn't shame him for needing it. But the blessing named here belongs to those who trust without that proof. Doubt isn't disqualifying — it's simply the harder road, and the one most believers actually walk.
entries.prayer: Lord, I have not seen, and I want to believe. Meet me in the not-seeing.

entries.reflection: This is an invitation, not a command. Christ doesn't tell the exhausted to try harder or explain the burden away — he says come to him first. Rest is where the answer begins, not a reward waiting at the end of solving everything yourself.
entries.prayer: Jesus, I come as I am, worn out. Give me rest.

entries.reflection: Renewal here belongs to those who wait, not to those who push harder — a hard instruction for a tired person, since waiting can feel like doing nothing. But strength that comes from waiting on God outlasts strength forced through on your own.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm tired in a way effort won't fix. Renew what I can't renew myself.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't say give thanks for everything, only in everything — a distinction worth keeping. You aren't asked to be thankful something hard happened, only to keep looking for what's good even while it's happening.
entries.prayer: Thank you, Lord, for this specific mercy today. Keep my eyes open for more.

entries.reflection: The reason given here isn't your circumstances but his character: he is good, and that endures whether or not the day went well. Gratitude anchored in who God is outlasts gratitude that depends on things going right.
entries.prayer: Lord, I praise you for who you are, not only for what you've given me.

entries.reflection: The instruction isn't to have no understanding, but to not lean the whole weight of a decision on it alone. Acknowledging him in all your ways is broader than prayer before a big choice — it's a habit in the small ones too, so the big one isn't a stranger to you.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't see the whole path. Make it straight where I can't.

entries.reflection: James promises wisdom will be given, and adds something easy to miss: without reproach. You aren't being scolded for not already knowing. Asking is treated here as the ordinary way wisdom arrives, not a last resort for people who should have figured it out alone.
entries.prayer: Father, I lack wisdom for this. Give it generously, the way you promised.

entries.reflection: The forgiveness asked of you here is modeled on one you already received, not one you're expected to generate from nothing. That doesn't make it instant. It gives you somewhere to start when your own kindness toward the person feels dry.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't have it in me to forgive this on my own. Lend me yours.

entries.reflection: Christ ties your forgiveness to theirs in a way that's uncomfortable to sit with. It isn't a transaction so much as a mirror: the grace you refuse to extend is, in some sense, grace you're refusing to fully receive.
entries.prayer: Father, soften what has hardened in me toward them.

entries.reflection: David prays this from what he calls the end of the earth — as far from help as he can imagine being. He doesn't ask to feel less overwhelmed. He asks to be led somewhere higher than where he stands, a request you can make even mid-collapse.
entries.prayer: Lord, my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I am.

entries.reflection: Christ doesn't tell you the future will be fine. He tells you tomorrow has its own trouble, and today's is already enough to carry — so you aren't actually required to carry both at once, however much it feels that way.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me stay in today. Tomorrow can wait for tomorrow.

entries.reflection: This promise is spoken to people in exile, not people about to be rescued tomorrow. God's plans for them play out over decades, not overnight — a durable kind of hope, built to survive a long wait rather than a quick turnaround.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't know your timeline, but I trust it has one. Give me hope for what's ahead.

entries.reflection: These words sit in the middle of a book about the destruction of Jerusalem — grief and hope on the same page. Mercy described as new every morning means yesterday's failure doesn't diminish today's fresh start.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you that this morning isn't bound by yesterday. Meet me new today.

entries.reflection: Paul writes this from a prison cell, which means the command isn't conditioned on circumstances going well. Joy here is something chosen and repeated — “again I will say” — not a mood that only arrives on its own schedule.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you for this gladness. Let it root deep enough to survive the days it doesn't come easily.

entries.reflection: James doesn't soften what jealousy produces: confusion and disorder, not just an uncomfortable feeling. Naming it plainly is the first step out of it — envy convinces you someone else's portion is a verdict on your own, which it never actually is.
entries.prayer: Lord, quiet the comparing in me. Help me want what you've given, not what you've given someone else.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't tell you to white-knuckle the desire into silence. He points to a direction to walk instead — the discipline isn't only refusal, it's replacement, filling the space with something that actually leads somewhere good.
entries.prayer: Lord, redirect what's pulling at me right now. Teach me to walk toward you instead of away.

entries.reflection: This isn't a description of a feeling but a list of actions, worth noticing when love feels complicated. Patience and kindness can be practiced even on the days the warmth doesn't come as naturally as it does right now.
entries.prayer: Lord, love through me today, especially in the small ways that are easy to skip.

entries.reflection: The contrast here is stark: resistance for the proud, grace for the humble. Pride isn't condemned for being confident — it's the posture of needing nothing from God, which is exactly the posture that shuts grace out.
entries.prayer: Lord, show me where I've been standing on my own. I'd rather have your grace than my certainty.

entries.reflection: Paul assumes there will be a complaint — “if any man has a complaint against any” — the grievance is treated as ordinary, not unusual. What's asked isn't that the wrong stops mattering, only that it stops being what you charge them for.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm still holding this against them. Help me set it down the way you've set down what I owe you.

entries.reflection: The psalmist argues out loud with his own soul, which is itself instructive — you're allowed to question the despair rather than simply accept it as the whole truth. Hope is spoken here as a command to himself, not a feeling he's waiting to arrive.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't feel much of anything good right now. Be the hope I can't manufacture on my own.

entries.reflection: The Preacher doesn't rank seasons — a slow one isn't a wasted one. If everything has its time, then even the flat, uneventful stretch belongs to something, whether or not you can see what yet.
entries.prayer: Lord, meet me in this dull stretch. Show me what it's for, or give me patience if I'm not meant to see that yet.

entries.reflection: David names the specific ache of this one: not a stranger's cruelty but a friend's, someone who ate at his table. Christ prays nearly this same psalm the night Judas betrays him — this wound is old, and it's one God has stood inside personally.
entries.prayer: Lord, someone I trusted turned on me. You know this pain from the inside — sit with me in it.

entries.reflection: The psalmist doesn't arrive at this confidence by comparison to anyone else — it's aimed entirely at the maker, not the mirror. Worth here is declared, not earned or measured against the person next to you.
entries.prayer: Lord, remind me I'm your careful work, not a rough draft. Quiet the voice that tells me otherwise.

entries.reflection: Christ's warning comes right after a man asks him to settle an inheritance dispute — the danger named isn't wealth itself but the belief that having more would finally be enough. It never quite is, which is the tell.
entries.prayer: Lord, loosen my grip on what I have and what I want. Let my life be measured by something other than what I own.

entries.reflection: James points to a farmer who can't rush a harvest no matter how much he wants to — some things only come in their own time, and pushing against that timeline mostly just wears out the one pushing.
entries.prayer: Lord, steady my heart while I wait. Help me trust your timing more than my own.

entries.reflection: Paul is careful to call this something learned, not something he arrived with naturally. Contentment here isn't pretending the hard state is fine — it's a skill built over time, one circumstance at a time.
entries.prayer: Lord, teach me to be content in what is, without giving up on hoping for what could be.

entries.reflection: This is said to a man about to lead a nation into a land he's never seen. The command to be brave isn't left to float on its own — it's anchored to a reason given in the same breath: God's presence, not Joshua's nerve, is what the courage rests on.
entries.prayer: Lord, go with me into what I don't know yet. Let that be enough courage for today.

entries.reflection: Paul names fear as something that can be given or withheld, like a spirit taking up residence — and says plainly it isn't from God. What is given instead is practical: strength, love, and a clear mind, the very things fear tends to crowd out.
entries.prayer: Lord, take back the fear that isn't from you. Fill that space with strength and a clear mind instead.

entries.reflection: The psalmist doesn't describe a quiet mind, but a crowded one — many thoughts, all at once. Comfort here doesn't arrive by silencing them all, but by something stronger moving in among them.
entries.prayer: Lord, my mind is loud today. Let your comfort be louder.

entries.reflection: Christ is specific about the kind of peace on offer: not the world's version, which depends on circumstances lining up, but his own, given as a gift regardless of how things currently look.
entries.prayer: Jesus, give me your peace, not the kind that depends on everything going right.

entries.reflection: This isn't a promise that grief is meaningless now, but that it isn't permanent. The image is tender and specific — a hand wiping away tears — not an abstract idea of comfort but a personal one.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't ask to stop grieving yet. I ask to trust that you'll one day wipe this away yourself.

entries.reflection: The verse doesn't rush the weeping — it's allowed the whole night. What it promises is that the night has an end, which is a different comfort than being told to stop crying now.
entries.prayer: Lord, stay with me through this night. I'm trusting you for the morning, even before it comes.

entries.reflection: James calls the person still standing in the middle of temptation blessed, not just the one who's already past it. Endurance itself is treated as worth something, not merely a means to an eventual reward.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm still in the middle of this. Help me endure the next minute, not the whole struggle at once.

entries.reflection: The help offered here comes from firsthand experience, not distant sympathy. Christ isn't advising from outside the struggle — he's able to help exactly because he's been inside one.
entries.prayer: Jesus, you know this pull from the inside. Help me the way only someone who's felt it can.

entries.reflection: The verse pairs two rescues that don't obviously belong together — the lonely and the imprisoned — as if isolation itself were a kind of confinement God specializes in opening.
entries.prayer: Lord, you place the lonely somewhere they belong. I'm asking for that place.

entries.reflection: Moses says this to a whole nation on the edge of a future without him leading it. The promise isn't that they won't feel alone, but that the aloneness isn't accurate — someone is going with them regardless.
entries.prayer: Lord, remind me you haven't left, even on the days it feels otherwise.

entries.reflection: The proverb hands you a lever, not a lecture: the same conversation can escalate or de-escalate almost entirely based on the tone of the very next sentence you choose.
entries.prayer: Lord, give me a gentle answer for the next thing I want to say sharply.

entries.reflection: Paul lists anger alongside slander and malice, not as a private feeling but as something with a public trail — the mouth is where it tends to show up first, and where it can also be caught.
entries.prayer: Lord, guard what leaves my mouth right now, before I've had time to cool down.

entries.reflection: East and west never meet, however far you travel either direction — the psalmist picks the one distance that has no measurable end, to describe how completely this is put away.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you for putting this as far from me as east is from west. Help me stop dragging it back.

entries.reflection: God doesn't ask you to pretend the stain isn't there — scarlet and crimson are named plainly. The invitation is to bring the actual color of it and let it be changed, not to arrive already clean.
entries.prayer: Lord, here is what's actually stained in me. I'm bringing it as it is, not as I wish it were.

entries.reflection: The image is of motion without direction — a wave goes wherever the wind pushes it next. Named plainly like this, doubt looks less like a moral failure and more like a describable, ordinary condition to bring honestly to God rather than hide.
entries.prayer: Lord, I feel tossed today. Steady me, even if the doubt doesn't fully leave yet.

entries.reflection: Faith is defined here as its own kind of evidence, not the absence of evidence. That reframes doubt: it isn't necessarily a lack of faith, but the ordinary condition of trusting something you can't yet see confirmed.
entries.prayer: Lord, I can't see the outcome yet. Let this trust stand in for the seeing, for now.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't promise the tiredness will lift immediately — only that stopping now would cost you a harvest that's still on its way. The instruction is to hold on a little longer, not to feel less tired while you do.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm tempted to give up right at the edge of something. Give me the strength for one more season.

entries.reflection: The psalmist asks the question out loud before answering it — a useful habit for a tired mind. Naming where help actually comes from is itself a small act of looking up.
entries.prayer: Lord, my eyes are tired of looking at the problem. Help me lift them to you instead.

entries.reflection: Thanksgiving here is described as a way in, not a reward for arriving. Gratitude is the gate itself, the ordinary way of approaching God rather than a special mood reserved for good days.
entries.prayer: Lord, I come to you today through thanks, not around it.

entries.reflection: The instruction covers everything, not just the obviously spiritual moments — ordinary words and ordinary tasks are included in the same breath as worship, if thanks runs underneath them.
entries.prayer: Lord, let even my ordinary tasks today carry some thanks underneath them.

entries.reflection: The promise isn't just direction but attention — God's eye is described as staying on you while the teaching happens, not a set of instructions handed over and left to figure out alone.
entries.prayer: Lord, teach me the way to go, and stay watching while I walk it.

entries.reflection: A lamp for the feet lights the next step, not the whole road ahead. That's a more modest kind of guidance than seeing the entire path at once — but it's enough to actually keep walking.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't need to see the whole road. Just light the next step.

entries.reflection: The two actions named — healing and binding — aren't instant fixes but the kind of care a wound actually needs: attended to, wrapped, given time.
entries.prayer: Lord, bind up what's still raw in me. I don't need it healed today, just tended to.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't ask you to decide the wrong didn't matter — only to hand the settling of it to someone else. Justice is still coming; it's just no longer your job to deliver it.
entries.prayer: Lord, I hand you what I want to settle myself. It's yours to deal with, not mine.

entries.reflection: Casting a burden is a decisive motion, not a gradual easing. The verse pictures a single act of letting go, followed by someone else doing the holding.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm putting this down in front of you now. Hold what I can't carry anymore.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't get the strength removed that he asked for; he gets an answer that reframes weakness itself as the place where God's power actually shows up best.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm weak right now. Let that be exactly where your strength shows up.

entries.reflection: Hope is described here as something that can overflow, not just barely last — abounding, not merely surviving. That's a higher bar than getting by, and it's offered as a gift rather than an effort.
entries.prayer: Lord, fill me with more hope than I need just to get through today.

entries.reflection: The claim isn't that every single thing is good, but that all of them are being worked together toward something good — a promise about the whole pattern, not a verdict on any one piece of it yet.
entries.prayer: Lord, I can't see the whole pattern yet. Help me trust it's being worked together.

entries.reflection: This is said to people weeping over a rediscovered law they'd failed to keep. Joy isn't offered instead of honesty about that failure — it's offered as the actual strength to move forward from it.
entries.prayer: Lord, let your joy be my strength today, not just my mood.

entries.reflection: The joy described here isn't tied to an event or an achievement but to a location — being in God's presence. That makes it available on ordinary days, not just the eventful ones.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you for the fullness of joy that's simply in being near you.

entries.reflection: Christ says this in the middle of hard teaching about pruning and abiding, not in a celebratory moment — joy here is meant to remain through the difficult instruction, not just after it.
entries.prayer: Jesus, let your joy remain in me even through the harder parts of following you.

entries.reflection: The proverb makes envy a physical cost, not just an emotional one — something that wears down from the inside rather than merely feeling unpleasant.
entries.prayer: Lord, give me a heart at peace instead of one that keeps comparing.

entries.reflection: Paul links envy to provocation, as though the two feed each other in community — envy rarely stays private, it tends to spill into how you treat the person you envy.
entries.prayer: Lord, keep this from spilling into how I treat them. Let me want good for them anyway.

entries.reflection: James pairs jealousy with a temptation to lie about it — to dress it up as ambition or standards. Naming it accurately, bitter and small as it is, is the honest first step past it.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me call this what it actually is, instead of dressing it up as something else.

entries.reflection: The blessing is aimed at the heart, not just outward behavior — a shorter, harder standard than simply avoiding the act, but one paired with a promise worth wanting: seeing God clearly.
entries.prayer: Lord, purify what I keep looking at and dwelling on, not just what I do.

entries.reflection: Paul reframes the body itself, not just the act, as something sacred and inhabited. That changes the question from 'is this technically wrong' to 'what belongs in this particular space.'
entries.prayer: Lord, this body is yours before it's mine. Help me treat it that way today.

entries.reflection: Job locates the discipline at the eyes, before the thought fully forms — a covenant made in advance rather than a resolution made in the middle of temptation, when it's already harder to keep.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me make this decision now, before I'm in the moment it's hardest to keep.

entries.reflection: The order matters: love here is a response, not an initiative you have to generate from nothing. Whatever love you have to give started as something given to you first.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you for loving me first. Let what I give away come from what I've received.

entries.reflection: Each verb describes love holding steady under weight — bearing, believing, hoping, enduring — not love as a feeling that comes and goes with the weather of the relationship.
entries.prayer: Lord, give me love that bears and endures today, not just love that feels easy.

entries.reflection: The image is of something unstoppable by ordinary forces — water is what puts most things out, but love here is described as outlasting exactly that.
entries.prayer: Lord, let this love be the kind that holds even when things get flooded.

entries.reflection: The proverb doesn't say pride sometimes leads to a fall — it treats the sequence as ordinary and expected, the ordinary shape of how this particular flaw tends to end.
entries.prayer: Lord, show me where I've gotten too sure of myself, before the fall does it for me.

entries.reflection: The proverb pairs each posture with what naturally follows it — pride trailed by shame, humility trailed by wisdom — as though the outcome were built into the starting point.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'd rather have humility and wisdom than pride and what follows it.

entries.reflection: Paul's instruction is concrete enough to act on today: not a general attitude adjustment, but a specific habit of considering someone else's standing above your own in this particular decision.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me consider them before myself in the next thing I do today.

entries.reflection: Christ ties your own freedom to the freedom you extend — setting someone else free from what they owe you turns out to loosen something in you too, not only in them.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me set them free from what they owe me. I think I need that release as much as they do.

entries.reflection: Christ places forgiving right inside the act of praying, not as a separate task for later — as if the two can't really be pulled apart, prayer and the grudge held at the same time.
entries.prayer: Father, I'm praying and still holding this. Help me put it down right here.

entries.reflection: Paul's qualifiers matter — 'if possible,' 'as much as is up to you.' He isn't asking you to guarantee reconciliation, only to make sure the block isn't coming from your side.
entries.prayer: Lord, let the block not be coming from me. Do what I can't with the rest.

entries.reflection: Each phrase admits the hard half honestly — pressed, perplexed, pursued, struck down — before adding the word that keeps it from being the whole story. Nothing here is minimized to sound better than it is.
entries.prayer: Lord, I am pressed right now. Don't let it be the same as crushed.

entries.reflection: The waiting comes before the rescue in this verse, and it isn't brief — patient waiting, not an instant answer. The pit is named specifically, miry clay and all, not smoothed over in the retelling.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm still waiting in the pit right now. I'm trusting you heard me already.

entries.reflection: Each exchange named is a straight trade for its opposite — ashes for a garland, mourning for oil, heaviness for praise. Nothing here suggests the heaviness was invalid, only that it isn't meant to be permanent.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm carrying a spirit of heaviness today. I'm asking for what you promise in its place.

entries.reflection: The instruction doesn't wait for a meaningful task to show up — it applies to whatever is actually in front of your hand right now, however small or uneventful it looks.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me put my whole effort into whatever's in front of me right now, even if it feels small.

entries.reflection: Paul redirects who the work is ultimately for, which changes how a dull task can be held — done for the Lord, it doesn't need to be interesting to be worth doing well.
entries.prayer: Lord, let this dull task be for you today, not just for getting through it.

entries.reflection: The verse says the same thing twice, waiting bookended around courage — as if the writer knows how easily the instruction gets forgotten halfway through a long, uneventful stretch.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm still waiting. Give me courage for the stretch that doesn't feel like it's moving.

entries.reflection: David is specific about why this hurts more than ordinary conflict: an enemy's attack he could have braced for. A friend's turn against him left no way to see it coming.
entries.prayer: Lord, I couldn't have braced for this one. Help me heal from a wound I didn't see coming.

entries.reflection: The proverb doesn't pretend every friendship holds up. It distinguishes between the many that might not and the rarer kind that does, and leaves room to still hope for the second kind.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you for the friend who stays closer than a brother. Help me trust again, carefully, in that kind.

entries.reflection: Joseph says this to the brothers who actually sold him into slavery — he doesn't minimize what they meant by it. He simply refuses to let their intention be the only thing that ends up mattering.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't know yet what you'll make of what they meant for harm. I'm trusting you're already working on it.

entries.reflection: The knowing described here happens before Jeremiah could do anything to earn or lose it — it precedes his birth, let alone his performance, which puts it outside the reach of his insecurity.
entries.prayer: Lord, you knew me before I could do anything to earn it. Let that be the ground I stand on today.

entries.reflection: The word used is closer to a crafted work than a random assembly — made with intention, for a purpose already prepared in advance, not figured out on the fly after the fact.
entries.prayer: Lord, remind me I'm your handiwork, made on purpose, not an accident you're still deciding what to do with.

entries.reflection: The verse doesn't describe God tolerating you at a distance but delighting in you up close, singing — a strange picture to hold next to the voice that says you're not enough.
entries.prayer: Lord, let me hear you singing over me today instead of the voice that says I'm not enough.

entries.reflection: The warning names the cost precisely: not the money itself, but the love of it, and the self-inflicted sorrows that follow those who let it lead them off course.
entries.prayer: Lord, show me where love of money has quietly taken the lead over love of you.

entries.reflection: The remedy offered for the love of money isn't more money but a different security altogether — a promise of presence that doesn't depend on what's in your account.
entries.prayer: Lord, let your presence be the security I reach for, instead of more.

entries.reflection: Christ doesn't ask you to feel differently about what you already love. He points out that the heart simply follows wherever the treasure is placed first — so the more useful question is where you're placing it.
entries.prayer: Lord, show me honestly where my treasure actually is, and help me move it toward you.

entries.reflection: The three instructions are given together, as if they support each other — hope makes the enduring possible, and steady prayer is what keeps the hope from running out first.
entries.prayer: Lord, keep me steady in prayer while I wait. Let hope carry the waiting, not impatience.

entries.reflection: The psalmist links impatience to comparison — fretting over someone else's timeline moving faster than yours. Rest is offered as the alternative to that particular kind of watching the clock.
entries.prayer: Lord, stop me from measuring my wait against anyone else's. Let me rest in yours instead.

entries.reflection: The Preacher pairs patience with humility, as though rushing to the end were itself a kind of pride — an unwillingness to let something take the time it actually needs.
entries.prayer: Lord, keep me humble enough to let this take the time it needs.

entries.reflection: Paul names contentment itself as a kind of wealth, not merely the absence of complaint — a short verse making a case that what you already have, held rightly, counts as real gain.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me count what I already have as gain, not as a placeholder for something better.

entries.reflection: The psalmist admits his own flesh and heart are failing him — this isn't written from a place of having it all together. Even there, what's left standing is described as enough.
entries.prayer: Lord, even when everything else in me feels like it's failing, be my portion.

entries.reflection: Christ doesn't say the other things don't matter, only that they aren't meant to be sought first. Discontent often comes from reversing that order — chasing the 'also' before the main thing.
entries.prayer: Lord, help me want your Kingdom first today, and trust the rest to follow in its place.

entries.reflection: Paul doesn't say suffering is good, or that it should be welcomed for its own sake. He says it isn't wasted -- that endured rather than escaped, it becomes perseverance, and perseverance becomes a tested, proven character, and that character becomes hope that doesn't disappoint. The chain only runs one direction: there's no shortcut to hope that skips the suffering and the endurance in between.
entries.prayer: Lord, I don't understand what this hardship is for yet. Help me endure it instead of just escaping it, and trust that you're building something in me I can't see the shape of yet.

entries.reflection: David doesn't pretend the fear isn't there -- he names it plainly, "when I am afraid," as something that will happen again, not a one-time failure of faith. The verse doesn't wait for the fear to pass before choosing where to put his trust; the two exist in the same breath. Trust here isn't the opposite of fear so much as what fear gets handed to instead of being carried alone.
entries.prayer: Lord, I am afraid right now, and I don't want to pretend otherwise. Take this fear from my hands before it takes root in my chest, and give me somewhere honest to put my trust instead. Even if the fear doesn't leave completely tonight, let it not be the only thing I'm holding onto.

entries.reflection: God doesn't promise Israel a life without deep water or fire -- he promises to be present in both, so that neither one overwhelms or consumes. The command "don't be afraid" isn't detached from the reason given right alongside it: you are mine, called by name, already redeemed. Fear loses some of its power once it's clear whose you are before it's clear what you're facing.
entries.prayer: Lord, before I ask you to remove what I'm afraid of, help me remember that I am already yours, called by name, not a stranger you happened upon. Walk with me through this water or this fire rather than lifting me out of it before I've learned you're really there. Let being yours matter more tonight than being safe.

entries.reflection: Moses says this to Joshua on the edge of a task that could easily undo him -- leading a whole people into a land he's never governed. The order matters: God goes before, then is with, then promises not to abandon, and only after all three does the command "don't be afraid" arrive. Courage here is downstream of being accompanied, not a substitute for it.
entries.prayer: Lord, go ahead of me into whatever is waiting on the other side of today, and don't let me walk into it as though I'm the first one there. Stay with me in the parts I can't prepare for, and don't let me mistake your quiet for your absence. Steady what discouragement wants to unsettle in me.

entries.reflection: The image is deliberately physical and immediate -- not a distant assurance but a hand actually holding another hand. Isaiah doesn't describe God pointing the way from far off; he describes God gripping tightly enough that letting go isn't really a live option. The help promised here is companionship first, solutions second.
entries.prayer: Lord, hold onto me the way this verse says you do, especially in the parts of today I'd rather not face alone. I don't need every answer right now -- I need to know your hand hasn't let go of mine. Help me, however that help needs to look, and let me feel steadied enough to keep moving.

entries.reflection: The psalm names the very specific fears that keep people awake -- the terror by night, the danger that comes without warning in daylight -- rather than speaking only in generalities. The picture of refuge under wings is deliberately small and close, not a fortress far away but a covering near enough to feel. Faithfulness itself becomes the shield, something proven over time rather than promised only once.
entries.prayer: Lord, cover me the way this psalm describes -- close, near enough to actually feel sheltered, not just told I should feel safe. Take the terror that comes at night and the danger I can't see coming in daylight, and be a shield between me and both. Let your faithfulness, proven before, be enough reason to trust it again tonight.

entries.reflection: John links fear specifically to punishment -- the kind of fear that expects to be judged and found wanting. Perfect love doesn't coexist with that particular fear; it displaces it, the way light doesn't share a room with darkness so much as end it. This isn't a command to stop being afraid by willpower, but a description of what actually happens as love becomes more complete.
entries.prayer: Lord, where my fear is really a fear of being judged and found wanting, let your love answer that directly instead of just calming my nerves. I don't want to manage this fear forever -- I want it genuinely displaced by knowing I'm loved without condition. Grow that love in me until there's less and less room left for this fear to live.

entries.reflection: Jesus doesn't dismiss the practical worries themselves -- food, drink, clothing are real needs -- but questions whether anxiety actually adds anything useful to solving them. The birds he points to next aren't idle; they're simply not carrying a worry that was never going to change the outcome anyway. Life being more than food isn't a denial of the need, just a reminder of what anxiety tends to shrink our attention down to.
entries.prayer: Lord, you already know what I need before I've finished worrying about it, so let me actually believe that instead of just reciting it. Loosen the grip anxiety has on my attention today, especially on the ordinary things I keep rehearsing that I can't control anyway. Remind me there's more to this life than the list of things I'm afraid of running out of.

entries.reflection: Jesus isn't promising tomorrow will be easy -- he says plainly it will have its own trouble. What he's addressing is the habit of borrowing that trouble early, carrying two days' weight inside one day's hours. Today's portion is hard enough without also being asked to hold what belongs to a day that hasn't arrived yet.
entries.prayer: Lord, keep me inside today instead of letting my mind keep sprinting ahead into tomorrow's problems before they've even arrived. Give me enough strength for what's actually in front of me right now, and help me leave tomorrow's portion where it belongs, in your hands and not mine yet. Don't let me carry two days of weight in the hours of just one.

entries.reflection: The word "cast" suggests a real, decisive action, not a gradual easing -- something thrown rather than slowly set down. David doesn't say the burden disappears, only that it's no longer his alone to carry; sustaining is an ongoing verb, ongoing support rather than a single rescue. Being "not moved" doesn't mean untouched by trouble, but not shaken loose from a foundation that holds regardless.
entries.prayer: Lord, I want to actually cast this onto you rather than just talk about doing it while quietly holding on. Sustain me through what today's anxiety keeps circling back to, in whatever practical way that needs to look. Keep me from being shaken loose, even if I can still feel the weight of what's happening around me.

entries.reflection: Proverbs treats anxiety as a literal weight, something with mass that presses a heart down and slows it. The remedy offered is almost startlingly ordinary -- not a theological argument, just a kind word, spoken or received. It's a reminder that comfort for anxiety doesn't always need to be profound to be real; sometimes it just needs to arrive.
entries.prayer: Lord, lift some of this weight off my heart today, even if it comes through something as small as one kind word from someone I wasn't expecting. Help me notice the ordinary kindness that's already around me instead of only the weight I'm carrying. And let me be that kind word for someone else who's carrying their own today.

entries.reflection: The peace promised here is conditional not on circumstances lining up but on where the mind is fixed -- steadfast, staying rather than wandering back to every worry. Isaiah doesn't describe peace as the absence of reasons to be anxious, but as what happens to a mind that keeps returning its trust to the same place. Perfect peace, in that sense, is less a feeling that arrives and more a direction repeatedly chosen.
entries.prayer: Lord, keep my mind steadfast on you today, because I know how quickly it wanders back to every worry the moment I stop paying attention. I'm not asking for every anxious circumstance to resolve -- I'm asking for the peace that comes from trusting you inside them. Keep bringing my thoughts back to you, as many times as it takes today.

entries.reflection: David describes this in the past tense, as something that already happened to him, not a theory about what God might do. Seeking comes first in the verse, before the answer and before the deliverance -- the fears weren't removed instantly on their own, but in the course of an actual search for God. It's a testimony offered so someone else afraid right now has reason to start seeking too.
entries.prayer: Lord, I'm seeking you in the middle of this anxiety, the way David did, and I'm asking you to answer the way you answered him. Deliver me from these fears, not necessarily by removing what I'm afraid of, but by meeting me while I'm afraid of it. Let this be something I can look back on and tell someone else about one day.

entries.reflection: The psalm pairs two images together -- healing and binding up -- the way a wound actually gets tended, not instantly closed but dressed and given time. It doesn't specify how long the healing takes, only that it's this God's particular work, aimed at hearts broken enough to need it. Grief isn't treated here as something to move past quickly, but as an injury worth the care of being properly bound.
entries.prayer: Lord, my heart feels broken right now, and I need you to actually bind it up rather than just tell me it will be fine eventually. Be patient with how slowly this is healing, and don't let me rush myself past grief that still needs tending. Do the kind of careful, unhurried work in me that this verse describes.

entries.reflection: Two words, and yet they carry enormous weight -- Jesus, standing at Lazarus's tomb, already knowing he's about to raise him from the dead, still weeps. This isn't a failure of faith or a lapse before the miracle; it's grief that's allowed to exist fully even alongside real hope. If Jesus wept knowing the ending, grief doesn't require pretending you don't know that God is good.
entries.prayer: Lord, thank you that you wept, because it tells me my own tears aren't a sign that I'm doing this wrong. Let me grieve honestly today without feeling like I have to rush toward hope before I'm ready. And when I am ready, meet me there the way you met Mary and Martha, still crying alongside them.

entries.reflection: Paul describes comfort as something that doesn't stop with the person who first receives it -- it's given so it can be passed along to someone else in their own affliction later. This doesn't ask grief to have a purpose it doesn't have yet, only points out that comfort received rarely stays only in one place.
